description: We are a creative and curious team passionate about space exploration, science, and technology. Through the NASA Space Apps Challenge, we aim to develop an interactive Martian map that highlights potential water resources, safe landing zones, geographical features, and environmental hazards. By combining research, innovation, and teamwork, we hope to create a practical survival guide that supports future human exploration of the Red Planet.
summary:
Interplanetary Martian Map – Survival Guide is an interactive Mars survival and exploration simulation built on authentic NASA satellite and telemetry data. Designed for future astronauts, mission planners, and students, the project transforms the Red Planet's harsh environmental conditions into an accessible, gamified decision-support system.

The platform maps critical Martian sites—including Korolev Crater, Deuteronilus Mensae, Arsia Mons, and Elysium Planitia—highlighting subsurface water ice reserves, radiation levels, and natural lava tube shelters. Users can seamlessly switch between 2D tactical maps and an interactive 3D globe mode, testing how dynamic day-night cycles and dust storm simulations impact solar power and survival metrics in real time.

Featuring multi-stage mission scenarios, real-time hazard alerts, and six-language support, this digital survival guide delivers an engaging platform for both STEM education and future Mars mission preparation.
details:
The project is developed entirely as a web-based, installation-free application using HTML, CSS, and Vanilla JavaScript. We utilized Three.js for 3D planetary visualization, a custom JSON-based localization structure for the multilingual interface architecture, and NASA's open-access Mars datasets (MRO, InSight, SWIM) for scientific data.

Rather than offering a static map, we designed a dynamic simulation where users try to survive through the decisions they make. Throughout the design process, we prioritized scientific accuracy, the direct impact of environmental variables (storms and day-night cycles) on energy production, modular and collapsible interface ergonomics, and global inclusivity across six different languages.

We selected one or more representative locations for every challenge you might encounter while surviving on Mars (such as Arcadia Planitia, Pavonis Mons, etc.) and adopted an interactive learning and hands-on experiential approach.It turned out to be a project that appealed to multiple audiences
